description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” — likely a probing performance metric — of six different multilingual BERT variants (mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, XLM-B₂) across nine language families or groups: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 30 with major gridlines at intervals of 10, and each bar is accompanied by error bars indicating variability or confidence intervals. The horizontal axis lists the language families in a roughly left-to-right order that does not appear to be sorted by magnitude. Within each language group, the six models are represented by colored bars: light blue (mBERT-L₂), dark blue (XLM-L₂), light green (mBERT-R₂), dark green (XLM-R₂), light pink (mBERT-B₂), and red (XLM-B₂), as indicated by the legend in the upper right. The IE-Indic group shows the highest overall effects, with XLM-B₂ reaching approximately 21 and mBERT-R₂ around 20. In contrast, the Isolate and Uralic groups show consistently low effects across all models, mostly below 5. The Semitic group shows moderate to high effects, particularly for XLM-B₂ (~20) and mBERT-B₂ (~15), while the IE-Slavic group shows a notable peak for mBERT-B₂ (~17). The chart suggests that model performance varies significantly by language family, with larger effects generally observed in IE-Indic and Semitic, and smaller effects in isolates and Uralic languages.
